title: Upper Egypt
capsule: Upper Egypt as a distinct political entity refers to the southernmost part of the Nile Valley — the narrow river corridor from the First Cataract at Aswan to the apex of the Delta — which in the period c. 2200–2050 BCE was contested between the declining Memphite Old Kingdom and the rising Theban dynasty. During the First Intermediate Period (c. 2181–2055 BCE), Upper Egypt fragmented among rival nomarchs before the Theban rulers of the Eleventh Dynasty under Mentuhotep II reunited the Two Lands around 2055 BCE. The attestation window here reflects the fragmented phase when Upper Egypt operated in practice as a separate political zone.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Upper Egypt as a distinct political zone during the First Intermediate Period is attested by royal titulary, nomarchal inscriptions, and archaeological evidence, but precise administrative boundaries between regional lords are difficult to map.
